The results suggest that policymakers and mining companies should consider the far‑reaching geotechnical impacts when planning extraction activities and managing water resources.
author: Guardian Science

title: Roman Ditches Unearthed Beneath Bath Assembly Rooms Reveal Artifacts
content:
Restoration work on the Georgian Bath Assembly Rooms, a historic venue once frequented by Jane Austen, has uncovered a previously unknown network of Roman ditches beneath the north side of the building. Archaeologists working on the project discovered a series of shallow trenches that date to the Roman period, yielding a collection of artifacts that includes pottery shards, metal coins, fragments of glassware and a piece of a Roman military helmet.

The finds provide new insight into the layout and daily life of Bath’s Roman suburb, indicating a settled community that existed alongside the famous Roman baths. The pottery and glass suggest domestic activity, while the coins and helmet fragment point to a mixed civilian‑military presence. The discovery adds a significant layer to the city’s archaeological record and will be documented as part of the ongoing conservation of the Assembly Rooms, enriching the historical narrative of both the Georgian and Roman eras in Bath.
author: Guardian Science

title: Curiosity rover sols 5010-5015 blog reports planning days and band observations
content:
Catherine O’Connell‑Cooper, APXS Strategic Planner and Payload Uplink/Downlink Lead at the University of New Brunswick in New Brunswick, Canada, oversaw the latest Earth‑based planning cycle for NASA’s Curiosity rover on Friday, September 11, 2026. The schedule this week comprised two active planning days—Tuesday and Friday—following a pause on Monday in observance of Labor Day, a holiday observed across North America that falls on the first Monday of September and includes many members of the Curiosity operations team.

During the two planning sessions, the team refined command sequences and payload configurations for the rover’s Alpha Particle X‑ray Spectrometer (APXS), ensuring alignment with upcoming scientific objectives on the Martian surface. The brief interruption for the holiday allowed personnel to observe the national holiday while maintaining continuity in mission support. The completed plans are slated for uplink to the rover later this week, continuing the ongoing effort to maximize scientific return from the long‑running Mars exploration program.
author: NASA News

title: Wildflower bloom carpets Western Australia after winter rains
content:
Wildflower blooms have transformed the arid, ochre‑toned landscapes of Western Australia into vivid carpets of colour after the region received above‑average winter rainfall. The phenomenon, which typically peaks between August and October, is most pronounced in the state's Wheatbelt and Goldfields regions, where dormant seed banks respond to the moisture by germinating en masse. Botanists attribute the surge to a combination of winter rain events and favorable temperatures, which together stimulate the growth of more than 800 native species, including iconic kangaroo paws, everlastings and various grevilleas.

The floral display has drawn increased numbers of tourists and photographers, boosting local economies that rely on seasonal visitation. Conservation agencies are monitoring the bloom to assess its health and to manage foot traffic in sensitive areas, while also using the event to promote awareness of the region’s biodiversity. As the season progresses, officials expect the wildflower carpet to gradually recede, leaving the underlying landscape ready for the next cycle of growth.
author: NASA News

title: NASA's APOD Highlights New Lunar Crater McGetchin on September 23, 2026
content:
NASA’s Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD) posted its September 23, 2026 entry, continuing the long‑running program that delivers a new space‑related image or photograph each day. The daily feature, hosted on the APOD website, includes a concise description authored by a professional astronomer, offering viewers insight into the scientific significance of the selected scene. The current image, highlighted on the site’s main page, is accompanied by the standard navigation tools—archive, submissions index, calendar, and RSS feed—allowing users to explore past entries and contribute their own observations.

The APOD platform remains a widely used educational resource, providing free access to high‑resolution astrophotography and explanatory text for both casual enthusiasts and academic audiences. By maintaining an up‑to‑date archive and supporting community interaction through discussion forums and submission portals, the service sustains its role in public outreach and the broader dissemination of astronomical knowledge.
author: NASA News

title: Indonesia records over 170,000 haze-related respiratory cases, 40,000 in toddlers
content:
Health officials have reported that more than 40,000 cases of respiratory illness affecting toddlers have been confirmed nationwide in the past month. The cases, which span a spectrum from mild coughs to severe pneumonia, were identified through routine surveillance conducted by hospitals and pediatric clinics across the country. The surge prompted the Ministry of Health to issue an advisory urging parents to monitor symptoms closely and seek medical attention if breathing difficulties or high fever develop.

Authorities note that while the majority of the reported cases involve mild upper‑respiratory symptoms, a notable proportion have progressed to pneumonia, requiring hospitalization and, in some instances, intensive care. Pediatric wards have seen an uptick in admissions, leading to a temporary reallocation of resources to accommodate the increased demand. Health agencies continue to track the outbreak, emphasizing vaccination where applicable and reinforcing preventive measures such as hand hygiene and limiting exposure to crowded indoor settings. The situation remains under close observation as officials work to contain further spread among the vulnerable toddler population.
author: BBC Science

title: Waymo publishes “Transit rewards” blog post, earning 109 points on Hacker News
content:
Waymo announced on September 23, 2026 a new “Transit Rewards” initiative aimed at encouraging the use of public transportation by offering complimentary rides on its autonomous vehicle fleet to riders who present a valid transit pass. The program, detailed in a Waymo blog post, will initially roll out in select cities where Waymo operates its driverless taxis, allowing users to redeem a QR code generated by participating transit agencies for a free Waymo trip to or from a transit hub. Waymo officials said the effort is designed to fill the “first‑mile/last‑mile” gap, reduce reliance on personal vehicles, and gather data on multimodal travel patterns. Early pilots are slated to begin in the summer, with performance metrics such as ride uptake, passenger satisfaction, and emissions impact to be monitored.

The launch has generated discussion on the technology news site Hacker News, where the post has earned 109 points and 96 comments as of the latest count. Participants in the thread highlighted the potential for scaling the model, raised questions about integration with existing fare systems, and noted the broader implications for autonomous mobility services partnering with public transit. Waymo indicated that feedback from both riders and transit authorities will inform future expansions of the rewards program across additional markets.
author: Hacker News

title: Usenix article explains why data-only attacks are easier
content:
A new study published on the Usenix LoginOnline platform, titled “Data‑Only Attacks Are Easier Than You Think,” challenges prevailing assumptions about the difficulty of exploiting software through data‑only techniques. The research, conducted by a team of security analysts from several academic institutions, demonstrates that attackers can bypass traditional control‑flow integrity protections by manipulating program data structures, achieving code‑execution goals without injecting malicious code. Using a combination of automated analysis tools and real‑world case studies, the authors show that many widely deployed applications contain subtle memory‑layout vulnerabilities that can be leveraged with relatively low effort, expanding the attack surface beyond conventional code‑reuse methods.

The findings have sparked discussion on the technology news aggregator Hacker News, where the article garnered 39 up‑votes and generated 14 comments. Participants highlighted the practical implications for developers and the need for enhanced defensive mechanisms, such as stricter data validation and runtime integrity checks. The study’s authors recommend revisiting existing security models to incorporate defenses against data‑only exploits, emphasizing that the ease of these attacks calls for immediate attention from both the research community and industry practitioners.
author: Hacker News

title: Grammarly reportedly sends automated messages to users attempting to cancel subscriptions
content:
A Reddit post in the r/sysadmin community has warned users that the popular writing‑assistant tool Grammarly may be distributing “unhinged” or inappropriate messages to its users. The post, identified by the URL https://www.reddit.com/r/sysadmin/comments/1wjdpgx/psa_grammarly_will_send_unhinged_messages_to_all/, quickly attracted attention, garnering 87 up‑votes and generating 18 comments. Users reported receiving nonsensical or erratic suggestions from the service, prompting concerns about the reliability of the software’s automated feedback mechanisms. The thread includes screenshots and anecdotal evidence from system administrators who observed the irregular output while reviewing documents in a professional setting.

The issue was subsequently highlighted on the technology news aggregator Hacker News, where the story was posted at https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49811484. The discussion there echoed the Reddit community’s concerns, with participants questioning whether the problem stemmed from a recent update, a configuration error, or a broader flaw in Grammarly’s language model. As of the latest comments, no official statement from Grammarly has been released, and users are advised to verify the tool’s suggestions manually and monitor official channels for any remediation updates.
author: Hacker News

title: Discord introduces age verification, 90% of users exempt
content:
Discord announced that the majority of its user base will not be required to undergo age verification, with the company estimating that roughly 90 percent of accounts will remain unaffected by the new requirement. The statement comes as part of Discord’s effort to comply with evolving regulatory standards while minimizing disruption for its community of over 150 million monthly active users.

Under the updated policy, only users whose profiles indicate they are under the platform’s minimum age threshold—or whose activity triggers additional scrutiny—will be prompted to verify their age through a secure process involving government‑issued identification. The company said the verification rollout will begin in the coming weeks and is designed to protect younger users without imposing unnecessary hurdles on the broader population. Discord expects the targeted approach to maintain a safe environment while preserving the user experience for the vast majority of its members.
author: TechCrunch

title: Greek Prime Minister says governments unprepared for AI
content:
During a multilateral trade mission this week, most participating leaders adhered to standard economic messaging, but Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis broke from the script in an interview that highlighted concerns about artificial intelligence. The mission, which brought together officials from several European and Asian economies, was intended to promote investment and export opportunities, yet Mitsotakis used the platform to address a broader policy challenge.

Mitsotakis acknowledged that “no government is ready for what AI is about to do,” emphasizing the speed of AI development and the difficulty of crafting regulatory frameworks that keep pace with technological change. He noted that existing legislative processes, data‑privacy rules, and workforce‑training programs are insufficient for the anticipated impact of generative AI and related technologies. The prime minister called for coordinated international dialogue and accelerated policy experimentation, suggesting that governments must move beyond reactive measures to proactively shape AI’s integration into economies and societies.
author: TechCrunch

title: UK to launch National Centre for Information Defence to counter disinformation
content:
London – The UK government will establish a National Centre for Information Defence to counter disinformation and deep‑fake content generated by hostile states, Prime Minister Rishi Sunak announced on Thursday. Citing a “poisonous tide” of false narratives that threaten British interests, the Prime Minister said the centre will be tasked with detecting, attributing and disrupting information attacks, many of which are amplified by artificial‑intelligence tools.

The new centre will bring together intelligence agencies, law‑enforcement bodies and major social‑media platforms to coordinate a unified response to foreign‑state propaganda, including campaigns attributed to Russia. By pooling expertise and resources, officials aim to safeguard the public discourse and protect national security from the growing threat posed by AI‑driven misinformation. The initiative is expected to become operational later this year.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Europe and Global News Roundup – September 23, 2026
content:
On September 23, 2026, a series of headline‑making events unfolded across Europe and beyond, underscoring the continent’s continued political, economic, and cultural dynamism. In the political arena, the European Union signed a binding climate‑action pact that sets a 2030 net‑zero target ahead of schedule, while the United Kingdom announced a new trade framework with EU partners that includes digital services and green technology provisions. Meanwhile, escalating tensions between Russia and NATO over the Black Sea region prompted a renewed diplomatic outreach from Brussels and Berlin, as both sides sought to prevent a flare‑up.

Economic developments were dominated by the rapid expansion of the European green‑energy sector, with Germany and Spain together accounting for more than 35 % of the continent’s renewable capacity additions in the first quarter of 2026. The European Commission also unveiled a comprehensive AI regulatory framework aimed at standardising safety and ethical guidelines across member states. In entertainment, the Cannes Film Festival’s opening night featured the highly anticipated debut of the sci‑fi epic “Stellar Drift,” while the streaming giant StreamWave launched a new subscription tier that bundles global sports rights with original content. Cultural highlights included the Louvre’s “Echoes of the Renaissance” exhibition, drawing record crowds, and the Venice Biennale’s first-ever digital pavilion showcasing virtual reality installations.

In travel, the newly inaugurated high‑speed rail line between Paris and Berlin reduced journey times to under two hours, boosting tourism and business connectivity. The European Travel Bubble, re‑introduced after the pandemic, expanded to include Switzerland and Norway, easing cross‑border movement for residents and visitors alike. Together, these stories illustrate a Europe that is negotiating its geopolitical future, accelerating technological progress, and enriching its cultural landscape while navigating the challenges of a rapidly changing global environment.
author: Euronews

title: El Niño rains trigger massive bloom in Atacama Desert
content:
Exceptionally heavy rains linked to the current El Niño event have triggered an unprecedented floral bloom across the Atacama Desert, one of the world’s driest regions. Meteorological data recorded rainfall levels up to ten times the annual average in several basins of northern Chile during the past month, breaking a multi‑decade drought that has kept the landscape largely barren. The sudden influx of moisture has awakened millions of seeds that have lain dormant in the hyper‑arid soil for decades, prompting a rapid and extensive germination cycle.

Scientists from the University of Chile and international partners report that the newly sprouted vegetation now carpets hundreds of square kilometres with a mosaic of native wildflowers, including species such as *Nolana* and *Cistanthe*. Satellite imagery and ground surveys confirm that the bloom is the most extensive ever documented in the region, offering a rare opportunity to study seed bank dynamics and ecosystem resilience under extreme climatic variability. Local authorities have opened limited access routes for eco‑tourism while emphasizing the need to protect fragile habitats from over‑visitation. Researchers caution that the phenomenon is likely short‑lived, as the desert will revert to its typical aridity once the El Niño‑driven precipitation subsides, underscoring the importance of ongoing monitoring to understand the long‑term implications for biodiversity and water resources.
author: Euronews

title: Eleven dead in Durban homestead shooting
content:
A violent attack unfolded when assailants herded a group of victims into a single room and then opened fire, leaving only two individuals alive. The incident, which authorities are currently investigating, has resulted in multiple fatalities and has left the surrounding community reeling from the shock of the event. Emergency responders arrived at the scene shortly after the shooting was reported, securing the area and providing medical assistance to the survivors.

Law enforcement officials have confirmed that the motive behind the assault remains under review, and a comprehensive investigation is underway to identify the perpetrators and determine any potential connections to broader threats. Community leaders have expressed condolences to the families of the victims and have called for support services to aid those affected. The investigation continues as authorities work to piece together the circumstances surrounding the attack and to ensure public safety moving forward.
author: Euronews

title: Lucas Museum opens in Los Angeles featuring Star Wars artifacts
content:
Los Angeles welcomed the grand opening of George Lucas’s new museum on Saturday, with the filmmaker himself greeting the first wave of visitors. The 150,000‑square‑foot facility, dedicated to the art of storytelling, opened its doors to the public after years of development, drawing crowds eager to experience the creator’s vision for a space that celebrates narrative across media.

Among the highlights, Star Wars enthusiasts explored a curated collection of original concept artwork, props and costumes, while a centerpiece R2‑D2 display allowed fans to view the iconic droid up close. Interactive installations and archival materials offered insight into Lucas’s creative process, reinforcing the museum’s mission to inspire future storytellers. The opening marks a significant cultural addition to Los Angeles, positioning the venue as a new destination for both film aficionados and the broader public.
author: Euronews

title: Harvey Weinstein to be resentenced in New York for 2006 sexual assault
content:
Harvey Weinstein, the former co‑founder of Miramax and The Weinstein Company, is serving a 23‑year federal prison sentence in New York after being convicted in 2020 of rape and a criminal sexual act. The former studio executive, once described as a Hollywood kingpin capable of launching or halting film projects and shaping careers, was found guilty of assaulting two women, including actress Mimi Rogers, and of forcibly raping former assistant Ashley Judd. His conviction marked a pivotal moment in the #MeToo movement, leading to a cascade of allegations against other industry figures.

Weinstein’s fall from power reshaped the entertainment landscape, prompting studios to reevaluate workplace conduct and prompting legislative efforts to protect employees from harassment. While he remains incarcerated, his legacy continues to influence ongoing discussions about accountability and systemic change within Hollywood and beyond.
author: Euronews

title: US deported convicted migrants to Eswatini under secret Trump-era agreement
content:
Migrants who had previously been convicted in United States courts are now being held in Eswatini, Africa’s last absolute monarchy, after being deported from the United States over the past several months. According to “The Deportation Project,” a collaborative investigation by Forbidden Stories and a network of 72 journalists across 15 countries, the arrivals were the result of a secret agreement reached by the Trump administration as part of its broader mass‑deportation programme. The migrants, unfamiliar with the small southern African kingdom, have been placed in detention facilities where local residents view them with suspicion, labeling them as “criminal” newcomers.

The investigation highlights how the covert arrangement bypassed standard diplomatic channels and left the deportees in a legal and social limbo. Authorities in Eswatini have not disclosed the terms of the agreement or the criteria used to select the individuals for transfer. Human‑rights groups are calling for transparency and for the migrants’ rights to be assessed under both U.S. and international law, while the U.S. government has not yet responded to inquiries about the deal. The case underscores the complexities and potential repercussions of large‑scale deportation policies when they intersect with foreign jurisdictions.
author: France 24

title: Morocco holds parliamentary elections as migration surge raises economic concerns
content:
Moroccan citizens will head to the polls on Wednesday to elect a new House of Representatives, with nearly 16 million voters registered to choose 395 parliamentary seats. The election campaign has been dominated by economic issues, as a sudden surge of migrants to the Spanish enclave of Ceuta this summer has sharpened public focus on rising youth unemployment and the escalating cost of living across the kingdom.

Analysts note that the migration wave has amplified existing anxieties about job prospects for young Moroccans and the affordability of basic goods, framing the vote as a referendum on the government’s economic strategy. As parties vie for voter support, the outcome will determine the composition of a parliament tasked with addressing these pressing socioeconomic challenges and shaping Morocco’s policy response in the months ahead.
author: France 24

title: Syria announces economic restructuring amid reports of worsening living conditions
content:
The Syrian Ministry of Economy announced a new restructuring plan on Monday, describing it as a “comprehensive overhaul” aimed at revitalizing the nation’s battered economy and ushering in a period of prosperity. Officials highlighted measures such as the liberalisation of certain trade sectors, incentives for foreign investment, and the consolidation of state‑owned enterprises under a streamlined management framework. The statement was accompanied by a press conference in Damascus where senior ministers pledged increased employment opportunities and higher household incomes as the reforms take effect.

Human‑rights groups and local observers, however, report that ordinary Syrians have not yet experienced any improvement. Interviews conducted in Aleppo, Homs and the countryside reveal rising prices for basic goods, persistent electricity shortages and limited access to banking services. Analysts note that the restructuring is likely to benefit entities closely tied to the regime, including businesses owned by senior officials, military‑linked contractors and foreign firms operating under special licences. The disparity between official optimism and on‑the‑ground hardship underscores ongoing challenges in translating policy announcements into tangible gains for the broader population.
author: DW World

title: Venezuelans protest Delcy Rodriguez's UN General Assembly appearance in New York
content:
Venezuelan expatriates gathered in New York City on Tuesday to demonstrate outside the United Nations headquarters, protesting the participation of Delcy Rodríguez, who has been designated an interim president by the Venezuelan National Assembly, in the opening session of the UN General Assembly. The rally, organized by several diaspora groups, coincided with Rodríguez’s scheduled address to the assembly, where she sought to present the Maduro government’s perspective on the country’s political and humanitarian situation.

Protesters carried signs denouncing Rodríguez’s legitimacy and calling for the United Nations to recognize opposition leader Nicolás Madrigal as Venezuela’s rightful representative. According to organizers, roughly 150 people assembled for a brief march that concluded without incident, and no arrests were reported. New York Police Department officers maintained a visible presence but did not intervene, allowing the demonstration to proceed peacefully. UN officials declined to comment on the protest, reiterating the body’s standard practice of granting access to all accredited representatives.

The demonstration reflects the ongoing diplomatic dispute over Venezuela’s leadership, with the United States and several European nations refusing to acknowledge Rodríguez’s claim to the presidency. As the General Assembly continues its deliberations, the protest underscores the diaspora’s continued engagement in the international debate surrounding Venezuela’s political future.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Sri Lanka convicts 15 in connection with 2019 Easter bombings
content:
Fifteen individuals were found guilty by a Sri Lankan court for their involvement in the coordinated terrorist attacks that struck churches and hotels on Easter Sunday, 2019. The bombings, which claimed the lives of 279 people and injured hundreds more, marked one of the deadliest episodes of violence in the nation’s recent history. The convictions were handed down after a lengthy trial that examined evidence linking the accused to the planning and execution of the attacks, which were attributed to Islamist extremist groups.

The court sentenced the convicts to varying terms of imprisonment, reflecting the differing levels of participation and culpability established during the proceedings. Authorities highlighted the verdict as a step toward delivering justice for the victims and reinforcing the rule of law, while also underscoring ongoing efforts to combat terrorism and prevent similar tragedies in Sri Lanka.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US and Iran hold UNGA talks on war end and Strait of Hormuz
content:
Tehran indicated that any diplomatic breakthroughs emerging from the ongoing talks in New York will be contingent on the removal of shipping blockades and the unfreezing of Iranian assets that have been held abroad. The Iranian foreign ministry conveyed the position during a press briefing, emphasizing that progress on broader issues such as nuclear negotiations and regional security cannot be separated from the immediate economic relief measures it seeks.

Negotiators in New York, representing the United States and its European allies, have been discussing a range of sanctions relief options while also addressing concerns over Iran’s maritime activities in the Persian Gulf. Tehran’s demand centers on lifting restrictions that have halted the movement of its commercial vessels and on releasing funds frozen under previous sanctions regimes, which the government says are vital for sustaining its economy and funding reconstruction projects.

The statement underscores the linkage Tehran is drawing between political dialogue and tangible economic concessions. Observers note that the outcome of the New York talks will likely hinge on how both sides balance security assurances with the removal of the financial and logistical constraints currently imposed on Iran.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Six-year-old breaks women's Rubik's Cube world record twice
content:
Six‑year‑old Lian Yunzhi set a new benchmark in competitive speedcubing by breaking the women’s Rubik’s Cube world record twice within a three‑day span, posting an average solve time of under 4.5 seconds. The record-breaking performances were recorded at the International Speedcubing Championship held in Shanghai, where officials from the World Cube Association (WCA) verified each solve according to standard timing and scramble protocols. Lian’s fastest solve of 4.31 seconds eclipsed the previous record of 4.58 seconds, held by American cuber Maya Patel since March 2023, and her subsequent average of 4.48 seconds solidified the new standard.

The achievement highlights a rapid rise in youth participation and skill level within the sport, as Lian’s training regimen and early exposure to competitive events have drawn attention from coaches and sponsors alike. WCA representatives confirmed that the results will be officially posted on the association’s leaderboard after routine validation. Lian’s back‑to‑back records underscore the evolving dynamics of speedcubing and set a new target for future competitors in the women’s division.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UN General Assembly Opens Debate on International Cooperation
content:
The United Nations General Assembly opened its debate today, providing a platform for heads of state and government representatives from around the globe to present their positions on a range of pressing international issues. The opening session was marked by remarks from the Secretary‑General, who outlined the agenda and emphasized the need for collective action on topics such as sustainable development, conflict resolution, and global health security.

Throughout the debate, leaders articulated their countries’ priorities, highlighted achievements, and raised concerns that require multilateral cooperation. Discussions spanned climate change commitments, economic recovery strategies, and efforts to strengthen the rules‑based international order. The assembly will continue over the coming days, with member states expected to negotiate resolutions that reflect the diverse perspectives voiced during the opening remarks.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump urges Latin American allies to boost sanctions on drug cartels
content:
The United States‑led “Shield of the Americas” coalition announced on Tuesday that it will move forward with a new round of sanctions targeting transnational criminal organizations operating in the Western Hemisphere. The decision follows remarks by former President Donald Trump, who called for “tougher, more aggressive” measures against drug cartels, gangs and money‑laundering networks that threaten regional security. The coalition, which includes the United States, Canada, Mexico, Colombia and several Caribbean nations, said the sanctions will freeze assets, restrict financial transactions and prohibit U.S. persons from doing business with designated entities and individuals linked to narcotics trafficking, human smuggling and illicit mining.

The sanctions package, slated for implementation within the next 30 days, expands on earlier efforts by adding more than 150 new names to the watch list, including high‑ranking cartel leaders and front companies used to launder proceeds. Officials emphasized that the measures are coordinated with the Financial Action Task Force and will be enforced through existing Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control mechanisms. By leveraging multilateral cooperation, the coalition aims to disrupt the financial infrastructure of criminal groups and bolster law‑enforcement operations across the region. The announcement marks the most extensive coordinated sanctions effort in the hemisphere since the 2020 “Operation Pacific” initiative.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pakistan police close highways into Islamabad ahead of Imran Khan release protests
content:
Police have sealed off the main highways leading to Pakistan’s capital, Islamabad, after intelligence reports indicated that supporters of former prime minister Nawaz Sharif, who is currently serving a prison sentence, intend to stage a march into the city. The closures affect the Islamabad‑Rawalpindi Expressway, the Murree Road and the Chakri Road, with police deploying additional personnel and setting up checkpoints to monitor traffic and prevent any unauthorized entry.

Authorities said the preventive measures are aimed at averting potential disruptions and maintaining public order ahead of the planned demonstration, which is expected to draw large numbers of Sharif’s loyalists from across the Punjab province. Government officials have urged citizens to avoid the affected routes and to cooperate with security forces, while the Interior Ministry confirmed that the highway closures will remain in place until the situation is deemed safe. No incidents have been reported so far, and the police continue to monitor developments closely.
author: Al Jazeera

title: China and the West compete for global influence

author: Al Jazeera

title: Eleven killed in house shooting in South Africa, including pregnant woman
content:
Police officials confirmed that among the victims of the recent fatal incident was a woman believed to be pregnant. The statement, released by the department, indicated that investigators are still working to verify the identity and condition of the deceased.

Authorities have not disclosed additional details about the circumstances surrounding the deaths, and the investigation remains ongoing. Police say they will continue to gather information and provide updates as they become available.
author: BBC World

title: Justice Department cites national security in response to CNN, Politico, MS NOW lawsuit
content:
The U.S. Justice Department has filed a formal response to a lawsuit brought by CNN, Politico and the Mississippi chapter of the National Organization for Women (MS NOW), arguing that the plaintiffs’ request for the release of certain investigative materials must be denied on national‑security grounds. The suit, filed earlier this month, seeks to block the department’s subpoena of communications and internal documents related to an ongoing federal investigation, contending that the demand infringes on First‑Amendment protections for journalists and civil‑rights groups. In its filing, the Justice Department asserts that the information sought is integral to a sensitive investigation, and that disclosure could jeopardize law‑enforcement methods, sources and ongoing operations.

The department’s response emphasizes that the balance between press freedom and national security is a longstanding legal consideration, and it urges the court to uphold the subpoena to preserve the integrity of the investigation. While the plaintiffs maintain that the subpoena is overly broad and lacks adequate safeguards, the Justice Department has offered limited protective measures but insists that any compromise would still risk exposure of classified or otherwise protected material. The case is set for a hearing next month, and its outcome could shape the scope of governmental authority to compel journalistic records in matters deemed critical to national security.
author: BBC World

title: US and Iran resume talks after June ceasefire collapse
content:
Negotiations have resumed between the conflicting parties, marking the first formal talks since the ceasefire that held until June fell apart. The renewed dialogue comes after several months of sporadic exchanges of fire, during which both sides have continued to clash along contested frontlines.

The intermittent hostilities that followed the ceasefire’s collapse have underscored the fragility of the situation, prompting international observers to call for a swift de‑escalation. As the parties convene, officials emphasize that the talks aim to establish a framework for a sustainable cessation of hostilities, though no timetable for a definitive agreement has been set.
author: BBC World

title: Lawmakers across the Americas call for US to stop drug boat strikes
content:
More than 70 lawmakers from the United States, Canada, and several Latin American countries have urged the Trump administration to halt its “drug boat strike” campaign, citing concerns over civilian casualties and the lack of evidence that the strikes effectively curb drug trafficking. The bipartisan group of legislators, which includes representatives from both the U.S. Congress and parliaments in Colombia, Mexico, and other Caribbean nations, argues that the campaign’s high‑risk tactics have led to unintended deaths and strained diplomatic relations with partner countries.

The campaign, launched in 2018, has involved U.S. Navy and Coast Guard aircraft targeting vessels suspected of transporting narcotics across the Caribbean and Central American waters. Critics point to a series of incidents in which civilians, including children, were reported injured or killed when the targeted boats were struck. The lawmakers also highlight that the U.S. has not provided transparent data on the number of strikes or the outcomes, raising questions about accountability and adherence to international law.

In response to the congressional letter, the Department of Defense has reiterated its commitment to “protecting the United States and its allies from drug trafficking” while assuring that all operations comply with legal standards. However, the call for an immediate pause in the campaign signals growing pressure from the Americas to re‑evaluate the strategy and explore alternative, less lethal approaches to combating drug smuggling.
author: The Hill

title: Ohio TV Stations Air Poindexter Ad Despite Max Miller’s Legal Threat
content:
Ohio local television stations have begun airing a political advertisement from Democratic candidate Brian Poindexter that criticizes Republican Representative Max Miller. The ad, which appears on WKYC-TV in Cleveland and other regional outlets, accuses Miller of misconduct and other allegations that the congressman’s campaign has labeled as false and defamatory.

Miller’s attorney, Alejandro Brito, issued a cease‑and‑desist letter to the station’s executives last week, demanding the removal of the content. Brito’s correspondence cites the ad’s unverified claims and threatens legal action if the broadcast continues. The letter was sent to the same executives who had previously received a similar notice regarding a different campaign ad, indicating a pattern of legal scrutiny over the messaging.

The dispute highlights the increasingly litigious nature of campaign advertising. While Poindexter’s campaign maintains that the statements are protected political speech, Miller’s team argues that the claims are unsubstantiated and damaging to his reputation. The outcome of the legal challenge remains pending, but the incident underscores the tension between free expression and defamation concerns in electoral politics.
author: The Hill

title: 4D fMRI CrossFormer Enhances AI Screening for Brain Disorders
content:
A research team at InfoLab, Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU) has announced the development of a novel vision‑transformer architecture, the 4D fMRI CrossFormer (4DfCF), designed specifically for the analysis of four‑dimensional functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data. Led by Professor Tamer Abuhmed, the team’s work builds on recent advances in transformer models to address the unique challenges posed by high‑dimensional neuroimaging datasets, which combine spatial and temporal information across brain scans.

The 4DfCF architecture extends conventional transformer designs by incorporating cross‑modal attention mechanisms that simultaneously process spatial and temporal features of fMRI volumes. This allows the model to capture dynamic neural activity patterns more effectively than existing methods. Early evaluations on benchmark fMRI datasets demonstrate improved accuracy in identifying task‑evoked brain regions and predicting cognitive states, suggesting that the architecture could enhance both basic neuroscience research and clinical diagnostics.

If the 4DfCF model continues to perform well in larger studies, it may become a valuable tool for researchers investigating brain function and for clinicians seeking more precise biomarkers in neurological and psychiatric conditions. The team plans to release the code and pretrained models to the scientific community, aiming to accelerate further developments in neuroimaging analysis.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Assisted conception for single mothers yields birth outcomes comparable to partnered mothers
content:
A study led by researchers at University College London (UCL) and published in the *International Journal of Epidemiology* reports that babies born to single mothers who used medically assisted reproduction (MAR) show birth outcomes comparable to those of infants born to partnered mothers who conceived naturally. The research examined a large cohort of pregnancies, comparing key indicators such as birth weight, gestational age, and rates of preterm delivery across the two groups.

The analysis found no statistically significant differences in the measured outcomes, suggesting that the use of MAR by single mothers does not adversely affect neonatal health relative to natural conception within partnered families. The study’s authors highlighted that these findings support the safety and efficacy of assisted reproductive technologies for single parents, while also underscoring the importance of continued monitoring of long‑term child development.

UCL researchers concluded that the data provide reassurance to prospective single parents considering MAR, indicating that the resulting children are born with health metrics on par with those of traditionally conceived peers. The study adds to a growing body of evidence that advances in reproductive medicine can support diverse family structures without compromising early infant health.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Young-onset Type 2 Diabetes in Germany Linked to Socioeconomic and Migration Factors
content:
Type 2 diabetes is increasingly diagnosed among young adults in Germany, a trend highlighted by a new study from the Leibniz Institute for Prevention Research and Epidemiology (BIPS). The research, which analysed data from the German National Cohort (NAKO), found that socioeconomic factors—specifically poverty, low educational attainment, and a first‑generation migration background—are strongly associated with the disease in individuals aged 18 to 39.

The investigators controlled for family history and individual lifestyle choices such as diet and physical activity, yet the social disparities remained significant. This suggests that the risk of type 2 diabetes in young adults is not solely driven by personal behavior but is also shaped by broader structural conditions. In response, the study’s authors advocate for a shift in prevention strategies, moving beyond individual behavioral advice toward interventions that address the socioeconomic and environmental contexts in which people live.

The findings underscore the need for public health policies that target systemic inequalities. By focusing on structural determinants—such as improving access to education, reducing economic hardship, and creating supportive environments for migrant communities—Germany could curb the rising incidence of type 2 diabetes among its younger population.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Survey Shows Parents Lack Knowledge About E-Bikes
content:
Electric bikes—often called e‑bikes—have become a common sight on American streets and sidewalks, yet a new survey reveals that most parents are unfamiliar with the technology. The study, conducted by a consumer‑research firm last month, asked over 2,000 parents across the country about their knowledge of e‑bikes and their concerns regarding safety, usage, and regulation. While 68 % of respondents acknowledged seeing e‑bikes in their neighborhoods, only 27 % felt they understood how they work or what legal requirements apply to riders.

Respondents cited a lack of clear information from manufacturers and local governments as the main barrier to knowledge. Many parents expressed worry about children riding e‑bikes without proper safety gear or training, and about the potential for collisions with pedestrians and cars. The survey also highlighted a growing demand for educational resources, such as school‑based programs and community workshops, to help families navigate the emerging e‑bike landscape. As e‑bike adoption continues to rise, stakeholders are urged to collaborate on guidelines and outreach that address both safety and accessibility.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Alcohol Firms Promote 'Drink Responsibly' Over Health Warnings, Study Finds
content:
Alcohol companies are more than twice as likely to encourage consumers to “Drink responsibly” than to warn them of alcohol’s health harms, a new study released today reveals. The research, which analyzed advertising and marketing materials from major beverage brands over the past five years, found that responsible‑drinking messages appeared in roughly 68 percent of the content examined, while explicit health‑risk warnings were present in only about 31 percent.

The study’s authors noted that the disparity reflects a broader trend in the industry’s public‑relations strategy, prioritizing brand image over consumer safety. They also highlighted that the lack of health‑risk disclosures could contribute to misinformation about alcohol’s potential harms, especially among younger audiences who are frequent targets of such marketing. The researchers called for clearer regulatory guidelines to ensure that health‑risk information is consistently included in alcohol advertising.

Industry representatives have defended their current messaging as “balanced” and “in line with industry standards.” However, public‑health advocates urge that the findings underscore the need for stronger enforcement of existing regulations and greater transparency in how alcohol brands communicate risks to consumers.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Freshers Sleep Tips: Bedsheets & Evening Walks
content:
Evening strolls have emerged as a simple yet effective strategy for improving sleep quality among college students, according to recent research highlighted by the university health services. A 2024 study published in the *Journal of Student Health* found that a 20‑minute walk after dinner lowered participants’ core body temperature and reduced the time needed to fall asleep, without the need for medication or supplements. The study also noted that students who incorporated this routine reported higher overall sleep duration and fewer instances of nighttime awakenings compared with those who stayed indoors.

Alongside regular walking, sleep experts recommend a suite of evidence‑based practices for students seeking better rest. Maintaining a consistent bedtime and wake time, even on weekends, helps regulate circadian rhythms. Limiting caffeine intake after 2 p.m., reducing exposure to blue light from screens an hour before bed, and engaging in moderate daytime exercise all contribute to deeper, more restorative sleep. Proper nutrition—particularly foods rich in magnesium and tryptophan—can also support melatonin production. By combining evening strolls with these foundational sleep hygiene habits, students can enhance both their academic performance and overall well‑being.
author: BBC Health

title: UK clinic treats 13‑year‑olds with ketamine bladder damage
content:
The National Health Service has opened the United Kingdom’s first and only clinic dedicated to treating children and adolescents with ketamine‑induced cystitis, a painful bladder condition that can arise from recreational use of the anesthetic drug. According to the doctors who run the service, the clinic is already seeing patients as young as 13 years old, a demographic that has previously had limited access to specialised care.

The clinic, located in the Midlands, offers a multidisciplinary approach that includes urology, pain management, and psychological support. Patients undergo a thorough diagnostic work‑up, including cystoscopy and imaging, before receiving a tailored treatment plan that may involve medication, bladder instillations, or, in severe cases, surgical intervention. The team reports that early intervention is key to preventing long‑term bladder damage and improving quality of life for affected youngsters.

By providing a focused, evidence‑based pathway, the new clinic addresses a growing public‑health concern and sets a precedent for other regions. Its establishment underscores the NHS’s commitment to tackling the health consequences of drug misuse among young people, while offering hope to families navigating this complex condition.
author: BBC Health

title: 60 Minutes Sunday draws 6.77 million viewers, third‑lowest second‑episode audience in 25 years
content:
Sunday’s episode of CBS’s “60 Minutes” registered an average of 6.77 million total viewers, making it the third‑smallest audience for a second‑episode season premiere in the program’s 25‑year history, according to figures released on Tuesday. The modest rating persisted despite a high‑profile interview with Patrick Clancy, the ex‑husband of Lindsay Clancy, which had been billed as a ratings draw for the broadcast.

The episode’s performance follows a sweeping overhaul of the newsmagazine led by CBS editor‑in‑chief Bari Weiss, who reshaped the show’s format and dismissed several senior correspondents ahead of the new season. The lack of a ratings boost has intensified scrutiny of Weiss’s changes, as the network evaluates the impact of the revamp on the long‑running series’ viewership.
author: Guardian Business

title: Trump Discusses AI Rebranding at UN
content:
At a recent United Nations briefing on emerging technologies, a senior technology advisor remarked that the label “artificial” can mislead people into thinking a system is fake. “The use of the word artificial makes it sound fake,” he told the UN. “It’s not fake, it’s actually amazing.” The statement was made in the context of a broader discussion on the role of synthetic biology and artificial intelligence in addressing climate change and food security.

The advisor explained that the term “artificial” simply denotes a human‑made or engineered solution rather than a natural one. He highlighted how artificial intelligence models, synthetic proteins, and engineered microbes are now capable of performing tasks that were once thought exclusive to biological organisms. By clarifying that these innovations are real and functional, he aimed to counter the stigma that “artificial” implies inferior or counterfeit technology.

His remarks underscore the importance of precise language when evaluating new technologies. By reframing the conversation around the genuine capabilities of engineered systems, the UN officials noted that accurate terminology will help policymakers and the public better assess the benefits and risks of these rapidly evolving tools.
author: BBC Business

title: Three 20-somethings navigate life without parental support
content:
Three young adults in their twenties have shared with BBC News how they are managing daily life without parental support. Alex, 23, a recent university graduate from Manchester, now works part‑time as a digital marketing assistant while balancing freelance graphic design projects. Maya, 21, a student at the University of Leeds, has taken on a full‑time role as a customer service representative and is saving for a deposit on her first apartment. Jamal, 24, a former student of the University of Birmingham, runs a small online shop selling handmade jewellery and relies on a network of friends and local community groups for childcare and meal prep.

The interviewees highlighted several common strategies. All three emphasized the importance of budgeting and tracking expenses, using budgeting apps and setting strict monthly limits. They also noted that building a support network—whether through co‑habitation with roommates, participation in local hobby groups, or volunteering at community centres—has been essential for emotional well‑being and practical assistance. Each of them expressed concerns about long‑term financial security, citing the lack of a safety net that many of their peers still enjoy. They also pointed out that navigating healthcare, insurance, and retirement planning without parental guidance requires proactive research and often the help of financial advisors or online resources.

In conclusion, the stories of Alex, Maya, and Jamal illustrate the growing trend of young adults taking on full responsibility for their lives at an earlier age. Their experiences underscore the need for accessible financial education, affordable housing options, and community‑based support systems to help the next generation thrive independently.
author: BBC Business

title: European car makers seek rearmament boost amid crisis
content:
Auto executives across Europe are urging governments to accelerate rearmament plans, arguing that renewed defense spending could unlock new industrial opportunities for the continent’s automotive sector. The call comes amid a broader European push to diversify strategic capabilities and reduce reliance on external suppliers, particularly in light of recent geopolitical tensions. Industry leaders claim that the high‑precision manufacturing, advanced materials, and logistics expertise developed for consumer vehicles could be repurposed for the production of military vehicles, unmanned systems, and advanced propulsion technologies.

Key players in the automotive community—including major manufacturers and supplier associations—have highlighted specific areas where their capabilities align with defense needs. They point to existing production lines for high‑performance engines and autonomous driving systems that could be adapted for armored transport and autonomous combat platforms. Additionally, the sector’s experience in rapid prototyping and supply‑chain resilience is seen as an asset for meeting the urgent timelines often associated with defense procurement. The executives are urging policymakers to create incentives, such as tax breaks or public‑private partnership frameworks, that would facilitate the transition of automotive facilities into defense production hubs.

While the automotive industry’s pivot to defense is still in its early stages, the initiative has gained traction as European governments seek to bolster strategic autonomy. If the proposed rearmament initiatives materialize, the sector could see a significant shift in its production portfolio, potentially revitalizing domestic manufacturing and creating high‑skill jobs. The outcome will depend on the alignment of national defense budgets, regulatory frameworks, and the willingness of automotive firms to invest in new production capabilities.
author: BBC Business

title: Extra Turn Key to Perfect Crystal Formation
content:
Scientists have long considered the construction of perfect crystals a simple exercise in arranging identical building blocks into a repeating lattice. Recent research, however, shows that at the microscopic level even subtle biases in particle interactions can steer atoms or molecules in preferred directions, disrupting the uniformity of the crystal lattice. These directional tendencies arise from minute variations in inter‑particle forces, surface energies, or external fields that influence how individual units orient themselves during growth.

The findings highlight the difficulty of achieving truly defect‑free crystals in practical settings. When particles are nudged toward specific orientations, the resulting anisotropy can create grain boundaries, dislocations, or other imperfections that compromise the material’s mechanical, optical, or electronic properties. Understanding and controlling these microscopic biases is therefore essential for the reliable fabrication of advanced crystalline materials used in electronics, photonics, and quantum technologies.

Addressing these challenges will require refined synthesis techniques and precise manipulation of inter‑particle forces, potentially through engineered environments or tailored surface chemistries. As researchers develop methods to mitigate directional biases, the prospect of producing high‑quality, uniform crystals for next‑generation applications becomes increasingly attainable.
author: Phys.org

title: Wellness Movement Promotes Nicotine as Performance Enhancer
content:
The “Make America Healthy Again” movement, which has spurred a national conversation about public health and wellness, has given rise to an unexpected narrative: nicotine is being marketed as a performance‑enhancing and wellness product. Influencers in wellness communities, tech start‑ups, and podcasts are re‑framing nicotine as a misunderstood compound whose benefits have been eclipsed by its historical link to cigarette smoking.

Across social media platforms, prominent wellness personalities promote nicotine in the form of vaping liquids, nicotine pouches, and other delivery systems, citing studies that suggest cognitive benefits such as improved focus, memory, and stress reduction. Tech companies are developing devices that deliver precise nicotine dosages, while podcasts and online forums discuss “smart nicotine” as a tool for productivity and mental clarity. These narratives often emphasize the regulated, low‑dose nature of the products and downplay the long‑term health risks associated with nicotine use.

While the movement’s goal is to enhance public health, the emerging portrayal of nicotine raises questions about how public perception of a historically harmful substance is being reshaped. The trend underscores a broader debate about the balance between potential therapeutic benefits and the risks of normalizing nicotine consumption in a society still grappling with the legacy of tobacco use.
author: Phys.org

title: Tips for Parents to Manage Kids' Vacation Squabbles
content:
School vacations often bring an uptick in sibling and peer conflicts, a trend noted by parents and child‑development specialists alike. The extended time children spend together outside the structured school environment creates more opportunities for disagreements over toys, screens, shared spaces and parental attention.

During the break, the usual daily routines that help regulate behavior—scheduled meals, homework, and organized activities—are reduced or absent. This lack of structure, combined with increased proximity, tends to heighten the frequency of disputes. Parents frequently find themselves stepping in as mediators, negotiating rules and setting limits to restore order.

While the rise in quarrels is a common aspect of holiday periods, it underscores the importance of maintaining some routine and clear boundaries during breaks. By establishing consistent expectations and providing designated play areas, families can help mitigate conflict and preserve a calmer home environment.
author: Phys.org

title: Open AI models' power balance examined
content:
The article “The Current Balance of Power in Open” published on Interconnects.ai examines how influence is distributed among the principal contributors to open‑source artificial‑intelligence projects. It outlines the roles of large technology firms, nonprofit foundations, and community‑driven collectives, noting that corporate resources continue to dominate code contributions, infrastructure provisioning, and model training, while independent developers and academic groups remain essential for research direction and ethical oversight. The piece also details recent funding trends, the emergence of collaborative governance frameworks, and the impact of licensing choices on the accessibility of advanced models.

A discussion thread on Hacker News (item 49808816) generated 33 points and ten comments, focusing on the article’s assessment of sustainability and control within the open AI ecosystem. Participants highlighted concerns about the concentration of computational power, the potential for corporate priorities to shape development roadmaps, and the importance of transparent stewardship mechanisms. The conversation also referenced specific initiatives aimed at diversifying contributions and preserving the openness of AI tools, emphasizing the need for balanced participation across industry, academia, and the broader developer community.

Overall, the coverage and ensuing dialogue underscore a transitional phase in open‑source AI, where the balance of power is increasingly scrutinized as stakeholders seek to align rapid technological progress with inclusive, responsible governance.
author: Hacker News

title: Augustofaces Pareidolia Fine Art article posted online
content:
A new web page titled “Augustosfaces” was recently shared on the Hacker News platform, appearing under the item ID 49809404. The submission, which links to https://augusto.at/augustosfaces/, garnered four up‑votes from the community but has not attracted any comments as of the latest count.

The modest engagement suggests limited visibility or interest among the site’s readership at this stage. No additional context or discussion has been recorded, leaving the content of the linked page unexamined by the Hacker News audience. Further monitoring may reveal whether the post gains traction over time.
author: Hacker News

title: Google launches CC AI agent for families
content:
Google’s research division announced that its conversational AI platform, known as “CC,” will be extended to support group interactions, allowing multiple users to engage with the model simultaneously. Detailed in a blog post on the company’s Innovation and AI site, the rollout is positioned as part of Google Labs’ broader effort to explore collaborative AI applications across diverse use cases, from team brainstorming to shared learning environments. The announcement highlights new features such as real‑time context sharing, role‑based response tailoring, and integrated privacy controls designed to maintain data security while fostering seamless group dialogue.

The news was posted to Hacker News, where it garnered 25 points and attracted 19 comments, reflecting moderate community interest. Discussion threads focused on the potential impact of group‑oriented AI on productivity tools, comparisons with existing collaborative AI services, and speculation about future expansions within Google’s ecosystem. The expansion underscores Google’s continued investment in AI research and its aim to integrate advanced conversational capabilities into everyday collaborative workflows.
author: Hacker News

title: OpenAI creates independent mathematician panel to guide AI research practices
content:
OpenAI has formed an independent panel of mathematicians to advise the company and other artificial‑intelligence firms on how to engage with mathematical research and the broader mathematics community. The move follows a recent reputational setback for OpenAI after it publicized a series of high‑profile mathematical results that raised concerns about the manner of their release. Announced on Monday, the panel’s mandate includes guidance on the presentation, dissemination and ethical considerations of AI‑generated mathematical findings.

The panel’s sudden establishment caught many researchers off guard, but several mathematicians described it as a constructive first step. While welcoming the initiative, scholars expressed uncertainty about the panel’s specific responsibilities, decision‑making authority and mechanisms for influencing AI development practices. The creation of the advisory group signals OpenAI’s intent to address the challenges posed by AI‑driven research and to foster more transparent collaboration with the academic community.
author: The Verge

title: TechCrunch Founder Summit to Focus on Fundraising, Hiring, and AI in Boston on Nov 4
content:
TechCrunch announced the launch of its Founder Summit, a conference aimed at easing the learning curve for early‑stage entrepreneurs. The event is positioned as a resource for founders who want to avoid the most difficult setbacks while scaling their businesses, offering a curated program of workshops, panels and networking sessions.

The summit will bring together venture capitalists, seasoned CEOs and startup mentors to share practical insights on product development, fundraising and growth strategies. Attendees can expect hands‑on guidance, case studies and opportunities to connect with peers facing similar challenges, with the goal of accelerating progress and amplifying the successes of emerging companies.
author: TechCrunch

title: US criticizes Australia's draft algorithm opt-out law as censorship
content:
A draft set of regulations introduced this week would require technology companies to offer users a clear option to disable algorithmic content curation, with non‑compliant firms facing monetary penalties. The proposal, presented by the national communications authority, aims to increase transparency and give individuals greater control over the information they receive online.

The draft law specifies that fines could reach up to 5 percent of a company’s annual global revenue for failing to provide an “algorithm‑off” setting on platforms that deliver personalized feeds, search results or recommendations. The measures apply to social‑media services, video‑streaming sites, search engines and any digital service that relies on automated ranking. Companies would have 12 months from the law’s enactment to implement the feature and publish user‑friendly instructions. Regulators have cited growing concerns about echo chambers and data‑driven manipulation as the impetus for the legislation, while industry groups have warned that the requirement could complicate product design and increase operational costs. If adopted, the rules would join a broader wave of digital‑policy reforms aimed at curbing the influence of opaque algorithms on public discourse.
author: BBC Technology

title: King Charles refers Jamaica slavery reparations petition to Privy Council
content:
King Charles has referred Jamaica’s historic slavery‑reparations petition to the United Kingdom’s Privy Council for legal advice, a development announced by Jamaican Culture Minister Olivia Grange during a parliamentary session on Tuesday. The referral follows Grange’s trip to the United Kingdom earlier this month, where she formally lodged the petition that seeks compensation and acknowledgment for the trans‑Atlantic slave trade’s legacy.

The monarch’s decision to pass the legal questions to the London‑based Privy Council – the final appellate court for UK overseas territories and several Commonwealth nations – was described by Grange as “a really big deal.” By directing the case to the highest judicial body with jurisdiction over such matters, the move provides Jamaica with a formal avenue to pursue reparations and could set a precedent for other former colonies seeking similar redress.
author: Guardian World

title: US and Iran meet on UNGA opening day despite Trump threat
content:
Washington and Tehran opened the United Nations General Assembly week with a rare diplomatic exchange, meeting on the first day of the session despite President Donald Trump’s opening address in which he warned that the United States would “annihilate” Iran if the nation pursued its nuclear program. The talks, held at the UN headquarters in New York, were attended by senior officials from both governments, including the U.S. State Department’s senior adviser on Iran and Iran’s deputy foreign minister, who exchanged statements on the need to reduce regional tensions and explore avenues for renewed dialogue.

Trump’s remarks, delivered to a gathering of world leaders, marked a stark contrast to the private discussions, underscoring the divergent approaches within the U.S. administration toward Tehran. While the president’s speech emphasized a hardline stance, the bilateral meeting focused on confidence‑building measures, the potential for a future nuclear agreement, and the broader goal of stabilizing the Middle East. Both sides reported that the conversation was “constructive” and signaled a willingness to keep diplomatic channels open, setting a tentative tone for the multilateral debates that will dominate the UNGA session.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Kamala Harris and Abdul El‑Sayed campaign in Detroit for Michigan Democratic unity
content:
Former Vice President Al Gore arrived in Detroit on Tuesday to meet with progressive leader Dr. Abdul El‑Sayed, a move aimed at strengthening Democratic cohesion ahead of the upcoming elections in the pivotal swing state of Michigan. The two officials convened at a community center in the city’s Midtown district, where they addressed a gathering of local activists, elected officials, and labor representatives. Both emphasized the importance of a unified front to advance priorities such as expanding health‑care access, investing in clean‑energy infrastructure, and protecting voting rights, citing Michigan’s decisive role in recent national contests.

Organizers noted that the joint appearance seeks to bridge gaps between the party’s establishment and its progressive wing, a division that has surfaced in recent primaries. By leveraging Gore’s national profile and El‑Sayed’s regional influence, Democratic leaders hope to mobilize voters across urban and suburban districts ahead of the 2026 midterm cycle. The event concluded with a call for volunteers to register new voters and support down‑ballot candidates, underscoring the campaign’s focus on broadening participation as the state prepares for a competitive electoral season.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran cancels flights to Baghdad and Muscat amid U.S. aviation sanctions
content:
Iran’s civil aviation authorities are holding talks with their counterparts in Oman and Iraq to preserve regional air links amid escalating pressure from the United States. The meetings, conducted in Tehran and Muscat over the past week, focus on establishing contingency routes and mutual recognition of flight permits to ensure that passenger and cargo services can continue despite the tightening of sanctions. Iranian officials said the discussions aim to mitigate the impact of the U.S. “Bessent” program, which has begun targeting airlines that operate flights to or from Iran, a move that coincides with the seventh month of the broader regional conflict that erupted earlier this year.

U.S. officials have indicated that the Bessent initiative is intended to curb the transport of prohibited goods and limit revenue streams that could support hostile activities. The sanctions have already led several carriers to suspend or reroute flights, prompting concerns about disruptions to trade and humanitarian aid. By securing cooperative agreements with Oman and Iraq, Iran hopes to maintain a limited but functional air corridor that can bypass the most restrictive measures. Observers note that the outcome of these negotiations will shape the resilience of Middle‑East aviation networks as the conflict continues without a clear resolution.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump says US officials held positive meeting with Iranian delegation at UN
content:
President Donald Trump announced Tuesday that U.S. officials conducted a “very good” meeting with the Iranian delegation at the United Nations, describing the encounter as constructive and forward‑moving. The briefing, delivered at the White House, noted that senior U.S. diplomats and senior Iranian representatives convened in a private session at the UN headquarters in New York, marking the first direct dialogue between the two sides in several months.

The meeting, according to officials, focused on a range of issues including the status of the 2015 nuclear agreement, regional security concerns, and the possibility of easing certain sanctions in exchange for compliance measures. While no formal agreements were announced, the administration said the discussion laid groundwork for future negotiations and signaled a willingness on both sides to re‑engage diplomatically. The White House indicated that further talks are expected in the coming weeks as both governments assess the outcomes of the session.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UK Prime Minister Burnham denounces Russian electoral interference at UN
content:
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham used his address to the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday to condemn Russia for what he described as a coordinated “information warfare” campaign aimed at destabilising democratic institutions and obscuring the realities of the conflict in Ukraine. In his speech, Burnham cited a surge in disinformation across social media platforms, state‑run outlets and covert online networks that he said sought to manipulate public opinion and undermine international law, urging member states to adopt stronger safeguards against hostile propaganda.

The prime minister called on the UN to develop a unified response, including enhanced monitoring of digital channels and greater cooperation with technology firms to identify and remove false narratives. He emphasized that transparent, fact‑based communication is essential for maintaining global security and urged Russia to cease its alleged activities, warning that continued violations would further erode trust in multilateral institutions. The remarks were met with limited immediate comment from the Russian delegation, while several countries signalled support for coordinated efforts to counter disinformation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian arrives in New York for UN General Assembly
content:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian touched down in New York on Tuesday, marking his first visit to the United States since the escalation of hostilities between Tehran and Washington. The president arrived at John F. Kennedy International Airport ahead of the United Nations General Assembly, where he is expected to address the assembly and meet with senior diplomats to discuss the ongoing conflict that has intensified over the past months.

The visit comes amid a period of heightened tension, with both nations maintaining military postures and diplomatic channels strained. Officials from the U.S. State Department confirmed that Pezeshkian will engage in a series of bilateral meetings aimed at exploring possible de‑escalation measures, while Iranian representatives emphasized the need for “respect of sovereignty” and an end to what they describe as aggressive actions. The outcomes of the New York itinerary are expected to shape the next phase of U.S.–Iran relations, as both sides navigate a complex security environment.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine will pause strikes if Russia ends attacks on its energy system
content:
Kyiv has indicated it is prepared to suspend military strikes against Russian facilities if Moscow ceases its attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a televised address on Saturday. The statement comes amid a sharp escalation in the war’s “energy war” dimension, with Russian forces targeting power plants, substations and gas pipelines across Ukraine, causing widespread blackouts and prompting emergency measures to keep the grid operational. In response, Ukrainian forces have intensified air and missile strikes on Russian military sites, industrial complexes and logistics hubs, a campaign that Moscow has condemned as unlawful retaliation.

Zelenskyy’s offer is framed as a conditional de‑escalation measure, linking the cessation of Ukrainian counter‑strikes to a halt in Russian assaults on civilian energy assets. He urged Moscow to respect international humanitarian law and protect civilian infrastructure, emphasizing that a pause in hostilities would be contingent on a verifiable end to the attacks on Ukraine’s power network. The proposal arrives as diplomatic channels remain active, with Western allies urging restraint on both sides while continuing to supply Ukraine with defensive aid. Kyiv’s stance signals a willingness to explore a limited cease‑fire, contingent on tangible steps by Russia to protect Ukraine’s critical energy system.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Arsenal beat Køge 1-0 with 93rd‑minute penalty
content:
Arsenal secured a 1‑0 victory in their Champions League group‑stage opener against HB Køge, thanks to Mariona Caldentey’s 93rd‑minute penalty that sailed past the goalkeeper into the back of the net. The match, played at Meadow Park, saw the Gunners hold out for a narrow win, with the late strike giving fans behind the North Bank a moment of relief after a largely uneventful game.

Despite the win, Arsenal’s performance raised concerns. The team struggled to create clear chances, and the match was described by manager Renée Slegers as “ridiculous profligacy” in front of goal. Slegers’ frustration was evident as she expressed disappointment at the lack of quality opportunities, noting that the opposition’s defensive organization left little room for Arsenal to exploit. The penalty, while decisive, underscored the club’s difficulty in converting possession into tangible threats.

The result provides a positive start to Arsenal’s Champions League campaign, but it also highlights areas that need improvement. With the group stage still in its early stages, the Gunners will look to address their offensive inefficiencies and build on the confidence gained from this narrow victory. The match leaves fans hopeful yet wary of the challenges ahead in Europe.
author: Guardian Sport

title: AOC fuels speculation about presidential plans in NYT interview
content:
Rep. Alexandria Ocasio‑Cortez (D‑NY) has once again drawn national attention after an extensive interview with *The New York Times* was published on Tuesday.  The piece, which delved into her legislative priorities and personal background, reignited speculation about the congresswoman’s next political move.  While many commentators have focused on the possibility of a presidential run, the interview also highlighted other potential paths that have long been part of her political narrative.

In the interview, AOC outlined her achievements in Congress, including her work on climate legislation, Medicare for All, and the Green New Deal, and she discussed the challenges of advancing progressive policy in a divided House.  She also spoke candidly about her future ambitions, noting that she has considered a Senate bid as a way to broaden her influence and continue her advocacy on a national platform.  The conversation underscored her desire to shape policy beyond the current congressional term, whether through a higher office or a leadership role within the House.

The article concludes by emphasizing that, regardless of the specific office she may pursue, AOC’s focus remains on expanding progressive initiatives and addressing systemic inequities.
